newsitem.title: USA: NYC underestimated revs by $325 mln -- NYS McCall.
newsitem.headline: NYC underestimated revs by $325 mln -- NYS McCall.

text.p: New York City officials underestimated revenues by $325 million in their proposed budget for fiscal year 1998, New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall said in a report Tuesday.

The report was issued as Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and leaders of the City Council intensified negotiations over the budget for fiscal year 1998, which starts July 1. The council also contends that the mayor underestimated revenues, which are determined solely by the mayor.
McCall predicted the city will end the current fiscal year with a surplus $80 million larger than expected. The Giuliani administration already projects an $856 million surplus.

McCall said unprecedented performance on Wall Street and more prudent planning by the city have brightened the city's fiscal outlook in the short term. But outyear budget gaps, starting with $2 billion in fiscal year 1999, remain a concern, he said.

McCall's revenue estimate adds pressure on Giuliani to increase his estimate for fiscal 1998. The city's Independent Budget Office earlier predicted that revenue was underestimated by $272 million, and the city comptroller reported that $202 million more in revenue would be available.

Council Speaker Peter Vallone wants to raise the estimate and create an additional $225 million "rainy day" fund that could be used to pre-pay debt for fiscal year 1999. The Council is also seeking tax incentives for "emerging" industries, reductions in the unincorporated business tax, and additional spending on some services, such as parks, museums and hospitals.
The budget must be passed by June 10.
